question: How far can the flash attention of a multi-row Gemma 4 verify block come down at long context?
model: Gemma 4 26B-A4B-it UD-Q4_K_XL, BF16 KV; MTP head mtp-gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-Q8_0
change: gemma4_attention_decode_flash_multi_kernel: one block per (token group, KV head, key slice) for a 2-16 row verify block outside graph captures; one thread per query-key dot product (eight-element vector loads), warp-reduced row maxima and denominators, shared V walk; groups up to 16 query rows. The single-token flash kernel (decode) is unchanged.

verify_block_ms.method: scratch: production runner, verify_dense_exact off, median of 8 after 2, rewind between

row_agreement_with_one_token_decode.note: a 9-row block after a 120-token prompt (129 keys, below this kernel's 256-key entry) has a row with KL 0.70 and one argmax change against one-token decode at a 0.43-logit near tie; present since 5823df24c (production expert arithmetic) and unaffected by this change

public_path_long_prompt.method: hipengine.LLM speculative_provider gemma4_mtp, budget 4, generate_detailed vs generate_speculative_mtp_detailed on one raw prompt of cycled campaign prose, 128 greedy tokens; decode phase = call less the shared prefill; draft acceptance 100% on this prompt

validation: tests/test_gpu_gemma4_flash_decode.py: multi-token launch within two bf16 ulps of each head row's scale against per-token launches (sliding/global, 2/5/9 tokens, 700/4096 keys)
cleaned kernel bitwise equal to the measured build at 8K/32K
limitations: Exact (strict) verify blocks attend each row with the single-token kernel and are unaffected.
